# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Policy

The manifesto outlines plans to reduce National Insurance for employees from 12% to 6% by April 2027, representing a £1,350 annual reduction for average earners. Self-employed individuals would see their main National Insurance rate abolished entirely. The party commits to maintaining fiscal rules requiring public sector debt to fall and borrowing to remain below 3% of GDP.

Business support measures include maintaining full expensing for capital investment, extending business rates relief for high street businesses, and raising the VAT threshold. The manifesto pledges no increases to corporation tax, income tax, or VAT.

## Immigration and Borders

The document proposes introducing a legal cap on migration with annual parliamentary votes on levels. Plans include continuing deportation flights to Rwanda, reforming asylum rules through international cooperation, and increasing visa fees. The salary threshold for Skilled Worker visas has been raised to £38,700.

## Public Services

NHS spending would increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 additional nurses and 28,000 doctors. Plans include expanding Pharmacy First services, building 250 GP surgeries, and establishing 50 Community Diagnostic Centres. Mental health support would expand to all schools by 2030.

## Housing

The manifesto targets 1.6 million new homes through brownfield development, planning reforms, and abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules. First-time buyers would benefit from permanent Stamp Duty relief up to £425,000 and a new Help to Buy scheme.

## Defence and Security

Defence spending would increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, with £10 billion invested in munitions production. The manifesto commits to continued Ukraine support and modernising armed forces capabilities.

## Energy and Environment

Plans include annual North Sea oil and gas licensing rounds, trebling offshore wind capacity, and building new nuclear plants including Small Modular Reactors. The party commits to net zero by 2050 while pledging no new green levies on household bills.

## Education and Skills

Proposals include mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds (military or civic), 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing underperforming university courses, and introducing the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education.

## Welfare Reform

The manifesto proposes reforming disability benefits assessment, tightening work capability assessments, and introducing stricter sanctions for long-term unemployed individuals refusing suitable employment.
